findings.description: A read-only viewer can modify expenses: POST /expenses/{id} is accepted (303 to ?flash=updated) and changes the title/category/amount, which also changes the shown total. Add (POST /expenses) and delete correctly return 403 for viewers, so the edit endpoint is missing the role check.
repro: POST /expenses/1 with title=HACK&category=meals&amount=1 using the viewer session cookie
Open /expenses: row 1 now reads HACK / $1.00 and the total dropped from $399.99 to $358.49

findings.description: A viewer can open the edit form for an expense by URL (200 with a full editable form and Save button), while /expenses/new returns 403 Forbidden for the same role.
repro: The Edit expense form is shown instead of 403

findings.description: The edit form does not preselect the expense's current category; the select always defaults to the first option (travel). Editing only the amount of a meals or office expense and saving silently changes its category to travel, corrupting data and the per-category filter and totals.
repro: Change only Amount to 70 and click Save expense
The list now shows Team lunch under travel

findings.description: Submitting invalid data on the New/Edit expense form (blank title, non-numeric amount, negative amount, invalid category) returns a 400 page with no error message at all, and the form is re-rendered empty so the user's input is lost and they get no hint what was wrong.
repro: Enter a whitespace-only title and amount 5, submit
A blank New expense form is shown with no error text and the typed values are cleared

notes: Totals and category filters were arithmetically correct; login errors, 404s, unauthenticated redirects and HTML escaping checked OK. Amount 0 is accepted (not reported). Browser UI testing was limited to the editor flows.

cost.notes: estimate from 26810 total tokens (85% cache read / 10% input / 5% output); range $0.0054-$0.0643
